title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-04
source: Audience Recording by Gerry Olsen. Sony TC-124 single-capstan portable cassette deck equipped with Sony F-99S One Point Stereo Dynamic Microphone IMP LOW (hand-held). 120 minute BASF normal bias tape. Lineage via Dan McDonald (droncit@yahoo.com): Master Audience Cassette->Nakamichi BX-1 (modified for flat transfer)-> Tascam DR-07MK2 (24-bit, 96kHz); DC8Forensics was used to apply the NAB curve for normal bias cassettes. Converted to 16-bit, 44.1kHz using 32-bit interpolation and a triangular high pass dither. After the NAB curve in a multifilter I applied a virtual vale and overtone generator for lost harmonics and used a channel blender to blend below 150 Hz to mono to minimize mic handling noise.

ai_review.summary: Superior audience tape of the legendary three‑part June 4 1970 Fillmore West show, with crystal‑clear acoustic and NRPS sets and a smoking electric set featuring the St Stephen > Midnight Hour > Not Fade Away sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording captures an iconic mid‑1970 performance in three sections—acoustic, New Riders of the Purple Sage, then electric—and reviewers rave about the clear, upfront audience sound (with a brief soundboard fragment for the first set). Musical highlights include the seamless St Stephen > Midnight Hour > Not Fade Away medley and the thrilling China Cat Sunflower → The Rider transition, while Jerry’s pedal‑steel work with NRPS and Mickey’s “non‑country country” drumming get special mentions.

ai_rating.rationale: Average rating across nine reviews is ~4.33; comments are consistently enthusiastic about both performance and tape quality, with only one mixed (3‑star) review.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audible audience recording praised for clear upfront sound; a short soundboard segment exists for the first set, but overall tape is considered superior and listenable with EQ adjustments.

standout_songs: St. Stephen > Midnight Hour > Not Fade Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑part show (acoustic, NRPS, electric) flows naturally; transitions especially praised, with the acoustic set setting a folk mood, NRPS adding psychedelic Americana, and the electric set delivering high‑energy blues/psychedelia.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Highlighted for his pedal‑steel work with NRPS and seamless switch from acoustic to electric guitar.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey's drumming described as ‘decidedly non‑country country’ on the NRPS set, adding a distinctive feel.
